clue.text: Ready to bully regular provider of income

parts.note: ready money, or the ready, is slang for cash
to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to intimidate a person who pays them regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably keeps bringing in money.

clue.text: Hard to get through audience interruption for singer

indicators.note: to get through means passing into the middle of the interruption

parts.note: a cough from the audience interrupts a performance
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A singer struggles to be heard past a spectator's coughing fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' looks like a vocalist but is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The chough is a crow-family bird, and crossword usage calls any bird a singer.

clue.text: Material in bad taste seen about

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the little word
bad suggests something spoilt, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fabric judged to be in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges TASTE into SATET, and 'about' puts it around IN; 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin, imitation satin fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Around charity event, breeze up to place of refreshment

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around or approximately
a fete is an outdoor fundraising event

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: air can mean a gentle breeze

explanation.surface: A breeze blows up round a charity fair towards the café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIR into RIA. A fete is an outdoor fair, often raising money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, a place where refreshments are served.

clue.text: Turner's work — transparent, isn't it?

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. Turner painted many pictures in a wash medium alongside his oils
asks what hue the liquid of rivers and rain has, and suggests it is clear

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Turner painting is see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner was a master of the paint medium mixed with H2O, and that liquid's own colour is clear.

clue.text: Bag, only one blows into it

parts.note: a sack is a bag
but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A bag, which is the only thing someone breathes into.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is an early trombone, a brass instrument played by blowing.

clue.text: Drink gingerly from vessel — it's not hot

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the vessel

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Drinking cautiously from a cup because it is not hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a cup but is a ship; 'not' drops the H, and 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sip is to drink in small mouthfuls, carefully.

clue.text: Trunk sportingly heaved about

parts.note: reads like luggage being thrown around, but describes a tree trunk tossed in a Highland sport

explanation.surface: A suitcase being thrown around for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber, a long pine trunk, is a Scottish Highland Games event.
explanation.definitionFit: The caber is a tree trunk thrown end over end at Highland Games.

clue.text: Howl, getting single thrust in the back from this?

definitions.text: Howl, getting single thrust in the back from this?

parts.note: to bay is to howl like a hound
one means single

indicators.note: in the back points to the last letter of the word thrust

explanation.surface: A victim howls on being stabbed in the back by a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the back' picks the T from 'thrust'; the whole clue also describes being stabbed by this weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is a blade fixed to a rifle, used for thrusting at an enemy.

clue.text: Check up about endlessly pressing author

indicators.note: about means going around, so the reversed check wraps the other piece
in a down clue up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to vet is to check

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: urgent means pressing

explanation.surface: A writer being checked over because something is urgent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns VET into TEV; 'endlessly' trims URGENT to URGEN, which 'about' puts inside TEV, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a 19th-century Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Where pest may be coming from, failing to conform

definitions.text: Where pest may be coming from
definitions.meaning: the letters of the word pest can be made by rearranging another four-letter word, so pest comes out of it
not in line with others, not keeping pace

explanation.surface: Tracing where some pest originates, and finding it out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not march in time with the rest is figuratively a nonconformist.

clue.text: Noble pig, about one year

indicators.note: about means going around, so the pig surrounds the year

parts.note: a boar is a male pig
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An aristocratic pig, roughly a year old.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyar was a member of the old Russian aristocracy, a nobleman.

clue.text: Dramatist is a catlike creature

definitions.meaning: Jean ... was a French playwright and novelist
a small spotted carnivore related to the civet, resembling a cat

explanation.surface: A playwright described as feline.
explanation.definitionFit: The French playwright Jean Genet shares his surname with the small civet-like animal of Africa and Europe.

clue.text: Old relative in journey makes border

indicators.note: in places the old relative within the journey

parts.note: a ride is a journey
gran, a grandmother, is a relative

explanation.surface: An elderly family member takes a trip that forms a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O + GRAN inside RIDE, splitting it after RI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande river forms part of the border between the United States and Mexico.

clue.text: Not paid to be brilliant

definitions.meaning: a debt still owing has not been settled

explanation.surface: Being unpaid but excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid bill is still owing, and an exceptional performance is first-rate; both senses share one word.

clue.text: Rage with clan set-to erupting in government building

parts.note: a storm is an outburst of rage

indicators.note: erupting means bursting out in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fury and a family fight breaking out inside a seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges CLANSETTO into ONTCASTLE, after STORM. Stormont Castle is in Belfast, home of the Northern Ireland Executive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont Castle in Belfast houses the Northern Ireland Executive, so it is literally a government building.

clue.text: Warning signal: amber pulsing in a series of lines

indicators.note: in places the shuffled colour within the other pieces

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so a series of them is several Ls in a row

indicators.note: pulsing means throbbing and shifting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An amber light flashing among rows of lines as a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulsing' rearranges AMBER to ARMBE, which 'in' puts inside A + LLL, after AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell rings to warn of danger, so it is literally a warning signal.

clue.text: Workers engaged by web designer not so intelligent

indicators.note: engaged by means employed inside, so the workers go within the designer

parts.note: a spider designs and spins a web
TU is the abbreviation for trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: Staff taken on by an internet designer are found to be less bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'web designer' suggests a website maker but is a spider; 'engaged by' puts TU inside after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupider is the comparative of stupid, meaning less intelligent.

clue.text: Brown Shirts turned up in China

definitions.text: Brown Shirts turned up in China

parts.words: Brown Shirts turned up in China
parts.note: reads like Nazi stormtroopers appearing in China, but means brown clay soldiers dug up there

explanation.surface: Nazi brownshirts unexpectedly appear in China.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownshirts were the Nazi paramilitary SA; here the 'brown' troops are of baked clay, and 'turned up' means excavated, near Xi'an in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: The army of fired-clay warrior figures was unearthed near Xi'an, so brownish soldiers were dug up in China.

clue.text: Swimmer's error — qualification not complete

indicators.note: not complete means only parts of the two words are taken, the run across their junction

explanation.surface: A swimmer's mistake left a qualification unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not complete' takes the end of 'error' and the start of 'qualification'; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rorqual is a baleen whale, such as the blue or fin whale, a large swimmer.

clue.text: Fail to get through Othello — it's more gloomy

indicators.note: to get through means passing into the middle of the name

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice
to die can mean to fail, as an engine does

explanation.surface: Failing to finish Shakespeare's tragedy makes one gloomier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get through' puts DIE inside MOOR, after MOO; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moodier is the comparative of moody, meaning more sullen or gloomy.

clue.text: One's drunk attempt to describe desert?

definitions.meaning: a tipsy speaker trying to say the word for desert ground, slurring its S into SH

explanation.surface: A drunk tries to describe the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk saying 'sandy' slurs the S to SH; shandy, beer mixed with lemonade, is also something one drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade, something one has drunk.

clue.text: Carthorse sees bird on branch, say, partly concealed

indicators.note: on means placed after, the bird sitting on what follows the perch
partly concealed means a piece of the word is hidden away, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a branch is an example of a perch for a bird
a heron is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A heavy horse watches a bird sitting on a branch, half hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly concealed' drops the H from PERCH, leaving PERC; 'on' sets HERON after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a large French breed of draught horse, used to pull carts.

clue.text: Keep time in Sanctus, showing passion

indicators.note: keep means hold, so the sacred word holds the time
in places the time inside the sacred word

parts.note: Sanctus is Latin for holy, the hymn's opening word

explanation.surface: Keeping in time during the Sanctus, sung with fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' and 'in' put T inside HOLY, after HO.
explanation.definitionFit: To act hotly is to do so with heat of feeling, passionately.

clue.text: Loiter in low church

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Hanging about in a Low Church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander aimlessly or hang about idly, a synonym of loiter.

clue.text: Dishearten daughter and another relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Discouraging one's daughter and some other family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt someone is to make them lose courage, a synonym for dishearten.

clue.text: By which to judge the theatre?

definitions.meaning: a standard against which something is assessed
the ... Theatre is a West End theatre at Piccadilly Circus in London

explanation.surface: A question about what standard to apply when assessing a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a measuring standard, and the Criterion is also a well-known London theatre.

clue.text: Run out of dairy product — it's still in the cow

indicators.note: out of means taken away from the dairy product

parts.note: curd is a dairy product; the reversed run inside the word product is a coincidence
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dairy has run out of a product that is still inside the cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops R from CURD.
explanation.definitionFit: Cud is partly digested food a cow brings back up to chew, so it is still in the animal.

clue.text: Put off getting head transplant, so passed on

indicators.note: a head transplant swaps the first letter for a new one

parts.note: delayed means put off or postponed

explanation.surface: A head transplant was postponed, so it was handed on to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting head transplant' swaps the first letter of DELAYED, D, for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A message relayed has been passed on from one person to the next.

clue.text: Elegist skewered by sick caricaturist

indicators.note: skewered by means run through, so the poet has the illness pushed inside him

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A poet of elegies run through by an ailing cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skewered by' puts ILL inside GRAY, after the G. James Gillray was a Georgian satirical cartoonist.
explanation.definitionFit: James Gillray was an English caricaturist famous for political satire around 1800.
